neighbours.label: obligation 'have to', strongest in 'having to' and 'will/going to have to' (fires on 'have'/'having' and the following 'to'); output suppresses need/must
fire: Nobody enjoys having to wait in line for hours at the post office.
Sooner or later, the city is going to have to fix that bridge.
Without a car, you will have to take two buses to get there.
She left the firm to avoid having to move to another city.
If prices keep rising, families may have to cut back on travel.
The players hate having to train in the rain during winter.
Eventually the company will have to explain where the money went.
He finished the job early, without having to ask anyone for help.
quiet: Nobody enjoys waiting in line for hours at the post office.
Sooner or later, the city is going to fix that bridge.
Without a car, you can take two buses to get there.
She left the firm because she wanted to move to another city.
If prices keep rising, families may cut back on travel.
The players hate training in the rain during winter.
Eventually the company will explain where the money went.
He finished the job early and had plenty of time for lunch.

notes: Card peaks ' have' x12, ' to' x11; output suppresses need/must. Probe: 'having to' 0.36-0.65, 'will have to' 0.22, 'had to' 0.09, possessive 'have' 0.01, 'need to' 0.05. Near misses drop the obligation.
